messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High runtime queue latency on cluster rdm-prod-rt-4. 95th latency crossed 8s, 5xx rate up by 4x in last 5m. Paging oncall.

maya (oncall): acknow. I'm on it. seeing backlog on /v1/generate and /v1/stream, inflight ~310 across pool (threshold 140). tagging rachel and tom.

rachel (eng-runtime): pulling traces and live spans. Early sign: a burst of large streaming connections + a model variant with large kv-cache regen is causing backlog. Also seeing many retry loops from a noisy client.

pagerduty-bot: Pager duty incident created (INC-2026). Primary oncall: maya.

jess (support): received about 12 customer complaints in the last 7m, include enterprise accounts: beta-labs, nova-ml. I'll send immediate ack.

tom (eng-sre): question: do we prefer to throttle or shed? My vote: quickly cap max_inflight per worker and add aggressive shedding for best-effort traffic. Then per-customer soft quotas for noisy customers.

maya (oncall): agreed. immediate mitigations: 1) runtime max_inflight from 256 -> 48 on rdm-prod-rt-4; 2) enable priority-based shedding (priority header present) and drop priority=low for non-logged requests; 3) add per-route rate-limits for /v1/stream and /v1/rerank for free-tier.

rachel (eng-runtime): will push via admin API; using feature flagging to minimize rollback friction. executing now:
```bash
# quick pulse-mode change
redctl admin runtime set --pool rdm-prod-rt-4 --max-inflight 48 --shed-policy priority --request-timeout-ms 10000
```

deploy-bot: runtime profile update initiated by rachel. change id: rp-5011.

rachel (eng-runtime): applying per-route limit for free tier:
```bash
redctl quotas set --route "/v1/stream" --tier free --rps 5 --burst 10
redctl quotas set --route "/v1/rerank" --tier free --rps 2 --burst 4
```

tom (eng-sre): also adding temporary customer throttle for nova-ml via quota service:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-admin/api/v1/customers/nova-ml/quotas" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_rps":8,"burst":16}'
```

jess (support): messaging queued to affected customers. sample: "We're throttling high-volume requests to stabilize platform health. We'll update when restored."

rachel (eng-runtime): metrics: queue depth dropped from 310 to 95 within 45s. 95th latency from 8.4s -> 1.9s for pool. error rate decreasing. good early signal.

anika (product): appreciate the quick mitigation. Are we dropping any high-SLA paid traffic? we should avoid impacting paid rerank if possible.

maya (oncall): we're prioritizing tokens by customer tier and request header. paid rerank preserved at the expense of free streaming. limited paid rerank reductions only for extreme clients. we applied targeted quotas to noisy customers only.

rachel (eng-runtime): note: after shedding enabled, a small number of workers reported increased GC cycles and ephemeral OOM events. investigating before scaling rollback.

tom (eng-sre): I see two nodes with sustained mem churn. I'll cordon and restart them gracefully, one at a time, to avoid capacity loss.

rachel (eng-runtime): starting rolling restart for the two nodes: rt-worker-21, rt-worker-25. command:
```bash
kubectl -n rdm-prod rollout restart deploy/runtime-worker --selector=runtime-pool=rdm-prod-rt-4 --grace-period=60
```

deploy-bot: rolling restart scheduled. ETA 5m.

maya (oncall): timeline note: incident opened 1802356000. first mitigations (max_inflight & shedding & free-tier caps) applied at 1802356078. restarts kicked at 1802356120.

rachel (eng-runtime): after restarts and caps, connections down ~35%, avg inflight holds stable ~60. 95th latency now ~1.6s. 5xx rate trending back to baseline.

jess (support): customers acknowledge. nova-ml replied: "We see improvements; please keep us updated."

anika (product): request we add a short status page blurb: "Intermittent high latency affecting streaming for free tier; mitigation in place." I'll publish a draft.

maya (oncall): handoff: I need to hand to tom for watch. I'll remain reachable for escalation until next check. tom, you own the incident from 1802356200.

tom (eng-sre): taking over. I'll keep monitoring for regressions and coordinate with rachel if we need to adjust timeouts or re-enable traffic.

rachel (eng-runtime): follow-ups to file in postmortem: 1) Make default max_inflight dynamic by route/model size. 2) Implement auto-shedding circuit-breaker that avoids GC/OOM cascades. 3) Improve per-customer burst detection and auto-throttling. 4) Add a "low-cost mode" for rerank that prefers compact quantized variants during congestion.

maya (oncall): also add: improve the admin API rollback path so we can revert max_inflight and shedding flags with single atomic call.

jess (support): will prepare customer-facing email and include timeline, actions taken, impacted customers list.

anika (product): scheduling a 30m incident review with runtime and SRE tomorrow. we'll decide on per-route default SLOs and tier behaviour.

tom (eng-sre): current status at 1802356360: metrics stable for 8m, 5xx near baseline, latency improved. Downgrading severity to sev3 and moving to monitoring. I'll keep a 1h watch.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026 status changed to "Monitoring".

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'm signing out. Please escalate if we see any re-spike. :white_check_mark:

end of thread.
